findings.title: The canonical digest rule collides above 2**53: distinct values produce identical RFC 8785 bytes, and the producer accepts an integer that JCS.parse refuses
findings.recommendation: Drop the `value == value.to_f` exemption in integer_to_s so every |n| > MAX_SAFE_INTEGER raises, making the producer's accepted set equal to the parser's; add one row to test/core_jcs_vectors_test.rb asserting the producer refuses what JCS.parse refuses. StateCodec already carries exact integers as ["integer", n] for callers that need them.

findings.title: The redaction rule is enforced by review only; DisclosableMessage's stated prohibition on interpolating third-party or provider text is contradicted by ProtocolError, and no test plants a credential in an error message
findings.recommendation: Add one row beside the existing rows in test/secret_sweep_test.rb: for each DisclosableMessage includer, build the message with a planted credential and assert the raised message matches none of Tamoz::Core::SECRET_VALUE_PATTERNS. No new class or module.

findings.title: The foundation gem hardcodes the domain vocabulary of the gems above it (four circuit scopes, every condition id, the intent watch type, the agent tool-error name mapping, a test-support HTTP framing helper)
findings.recommendation: Leave the code; record the Circuit::Registry exception explicitly in gems/tamoz-core/README.md beside the "no graph, persistence, provider, network, or model behavior" claim, naming it as the one intentional domain table and why.

findings.title: The pinned public-surface contract names 49 tamoz-core constants and omits the values every sibling gem actually consumes (the whole Circuit surface, Core.deep_dup, Core.jcs/digest/verify_digest, Capability::*, SituationRecall::*, TurnContext, StoreEntry)
findings.recommendation: Reconcile the pinned list with the set sibling gems actually reference; add the consumed names to the existing tamoz-core block rather than introducing a new contract mechanism.

findings.title: MAX_REGISTRATIONS (256) is unreachable through add_registration, which copies the registration list on every call; only a 257-entry construction can trip it
findings.recommendation: Restate the cap where an incremental caller meets it, or record in the existing comment that tag-pattern and duplicate-tag refusal fire first; no structural change.

findings.title: A stored circuit record's threshold and probe_window_ms load without being bound to the registry scope, although every other record dimension is policy-checked on load
findings.recommendation: In validate_scalars!, where scope is already in hand via validate!, compare payload["threshold"] to scope.threshold and payload["probe_window_ms"] to scope.probe_window_ms, raising CheckpointCorruptionError like the neighbouring checks.

findings.title: Prior finding 058: the deep_freeze rejection still holds on substance (key types are silently changed), but the recorded reason does not reproduce -- **Core.deep_freeze into a keyword receiver succeeds on Ruby 3.3.11, it does not raise
findings.recommendation: None. The rejection and both flag halves are confirmed; only the historical note's stated reason needs correcting.
